title: Trace and base-change rearrangement before the first triangle
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$. Schemes are separated finite-type $k$-schemes and morphisms are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Write $R_Z=\mathcal O_{E,Z}$ for the pulled-back condensed coefficient ring, $D(Z)=D(\Mod_{R_Z})$ for its unbounded derived category [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], and $\mathcal L(Z)=\Loc(\Dbc(Z,\mathcal O_E))$ [sk-def-sfb-constructible, sk-def-localizing-closure]. Pullbacks and direct images are the canonical derived functors with adjunction $h^*\dashv Rh_*$ [def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull-adjunction], and pullback coefficients are identified by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. All tensors are derived tensors over $R_Z$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. For a proper $h:Z\to B$, let $\pi_{h,L,N}:L\otimes Rh_*N\to Rh_*(h^*L\otimes N)$ be the canonical projection map, the adjoint transpose of $1\otimes c_{h,N}$, where $c_h$ is the canonical counit.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be proper, let $W=X\times_YX$ with projections $p_1,p_2$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], and use the canonical identification $fp_1=fp_2$. Put $T_Y=R_Y(1)[2]$, $T_X=f^*T_Y$, and $T_W=p_1^*T_X=p_2^*T_X$, with twists as in [sk-def-sp-tate-twist] and pullback/tensor comparisons as in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Let $b_2:f^*Rf_*\to Rp_{2*}p_1^*$ and $b_1:f^*Rf_*\to Rp_{1*}p_2^*$ be the canonical base-change mates [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Assume these and the projection maps used below are isomorphisms on $\mathcal L$ and that the displayed functors preserve $\mathcal L$. Take morphisms $t:Rf_*T_X\to R_Y$ and $t_i:Rp_{i*}T_W\to R_X$ satisfying $t_i\circ b_{i,T_X}=f^*t$ for $i=1,2$. Define $G(K)=f^*K\otimes T_X$ and
$$e_K=(1_K\otimes t)\circ\pi_{f,K,T_X}^{-1}:Rf_*GK\to K.$$
For $N\in\mathcal L(X)$ define the natural isomorphism
$$B_N:Rp_{2*}(p_1^*N\otimes T_W)\xrightarrow{\pi_{p_2,T_X,p_1^*N}^{-1}}Rp_{2*}p_1^*N\otimes T_X\xrightarrow{b_{2,N}^{-1}\otimes1}GRf_*N,$$
where the first arrow uses the canonical tensor symmetries.

For every $N\in\mathcal L(X)$ one has
$$e_{Rf_*N}\circ Rf_*(B_N)=Rf_*(1_N\otimes t_1)\circ Rf_*(\pi_{p_1,N,T_W}^{-1}).$$
The source of the left side is $Rf_*Rp_{2*}(p_1^*N\otimes T_W)$; that of the right side is identified with it by $Rf_*Rp_{2*}\simeq R(fp_2)_*=R(fp_1)_*\simeq Rf_*Rp_{1*}$. Both targets are $Rf_*N$.

proof.text: Use the total module operations [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], their canonical adjunction [def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull-adjunction], and Cartesian coefficients [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] on small pro-etale sites. The normalized tensor, symmetry and composite-adjunction comparisons of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] apply to these ordinary ringed-topos operations. Put $P=Rf_*$, $F=f^*$, $Q_i=Rp_{i*}$, $U_i=p_i^*$, $T=T_X$, $A=PN$, $C=PT$, $H=U_1N\otimes U_2T$. The specified square comparison is monoidal and its conjugate identifies $PQ_1=Rh_*=PQ_2$ for $h=fp_1=fp_2$; also $U_1T=U_2T=T_W$.

source.place: Tags 07A4, 0D6D, 07A6 and 0D6E: tensor, pullback composition, adjunction and direct-image composition

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-kunneth-factorizations] with $q=f$, $a=p_1$, $b=p_2$, the commutation $fp_1\cong fp_2$ of step 1, its $M$ equal to $N$ and its $N$ equal to $T$. Its mates $\beta,\bar\beta$ are $b_2,b_1$, and its $RU\cong RS$ is the specified identification $PQ_2=Rh_*=PQ_1$. Write $\lambda_{u;E,L}:Ru_*E\otimes L\to Ru_*(E\otimes u^*L)$ for the projection map in direct-image-first order, the adjunct of $c_{u,E}\otimes1$. By the symmetric monoidality of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons], $\lambda_{u;E,L}$ is $\pi_{u,L,E}$ conjugated by the two tensor symmetries, since both have the same transpose. So the two composites of that lemma are
$$D_2=P(\lambda_{p_2;U_1N,T})P(b_{2,N}\otimes1)\pi_{f,A,T},\quad D_1=P(\pi_{p_1,N,T_W})P(1\otimes b_{1,T})\lambda_{f;N,C},$$
and the lemma gives $D_1=D_2:A\otimes C\to Rh_*H$ under that identification. Since $B_N=(b_{2,N}^{-1}\otimes1)\lambda_{p_2;U_1N,T}^{-1}$, cancellation gives $P(B_N)D_2=\pi_{f,A,T}$. Thus $D_2$ is invertible by the assumed isomorphisms; no invertibility of $\lambda_{f;N,C}$ is needed.

source.place: First identity: equality of the two projection/exchange factorizations, specialized to the square $W=X\times_YX$ of det-thm-int-restriction-line (1), first triangle

proof.text:
Precomposing the required left side with $D_2$ gives $e_A P(B_N)D_2=e_A\pi_{f,A,T}=1_A\otimes t$. For the right side use $D_1=D_2$ and cancel $P(\pi_{p_1,N,T_W}^{-1})$ against its forward factor. The result is
$$P(1_N\otimes t_1)P(\pi_{p_1,N,T_W}^{-1})D_1=P(1_N\otimes(t_1b_{1,T}))\lambda_{f;N,C}=P(1_N\otimes F(t))\lambda_{f;N,C}.$$
The last equality is the given trace base-change equation. Naturality in the scalar input from [lem-sfb-ringed-projection-tensor-composition] identifies this with $\lambda_{f;N,R_Y}(1_A\otimes t)$. The tensor-unit normalization from [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] makes this $1_A\otimes t$, using $FR_Y=R_X$ and the canonical unitors.
